rationale: Tests understanding of the pathophysiological consequence of dopamine loss in the indirect pathway, a core TRAP concept.
Tests classification of tremor type — the most critical distinction separating parkinsonian (rest) from essential (postural/kinetic) tremor.
Applies the phenomenological classification framework to distinguish hyperkinetic movement disorders — chorea vs dystonia vs tics vs myoclonus.

Tests understanding of the pharmacological management principle that drug class is determined by phenomenological classification — especially the danger of dopamine antagonists in parkinsonian syndromes.
Tests the critical examination technique distinction — the pull test assesses postural instability, which defines UPDRS Hoehn and Yahr Stage 3.
Tests ability to interpret UPDRS Part III scores and MDS clinical diagnostic criteria to distinguish idiopathic PD from Parkinson-plus syndromes — a key clinical synthesis skill.
Tests the diagnostic formulation principle that Wilson's disease must be excluded in any young patient (<50 years) with movement disorder before attributing it to another cause.
Tests recognition of drug-induced movement disorders — a common and reversible cause that must be considered in clinical formulation.
Tests the selection principle for DaTscan vs MRI in movement disorder workup — imaging is often ordered incorrectly in PD.
Tests the key diagnostic fact about Kayser-Fleischer rings and ceruloplasmin in Wilson's disease workup — critical because Wilson's is treatable and often missed.
Tests understanding of levodopa motor complications — wearing-off vs peak-dose dyskinesia — as the most clinically important long-term pharmacotherapy challenge in PD.
Tests the critical drug interaction fact — combining levodopa with non-selective MAO inhibitors causes hypertensive crisis, a high-stakes pharmacotherapy safety trap.
